title: Tool page
summary: A page that takes input, runs one action and shows the outcome: input fields, a Run button, and a stat, table, code block or line of text once it finishes. Set the run(values) callback as a property (business logic, never config data) - it may reject, which shows the built-in error state with Retry.

props.name: config
props.description: { input: [{ key, type: 'text'|'email'|'number'|'date'|'textarea'|'select', label, placeholder?, required?, options?, hint? }], outcome: 'stat'|'table'|'code'|'text' }. input builds one labelled control per field (a hint, or help, adds an info button beside the label that opens a tooltip) (a select's options are [{ value, label? }] or plain strings); outcome picks what the run() result draws as: stat (Object.assign onto pk-stat: value, label, ...), table ({ columns, rows } onto pk-table), code (a string, or { code } onto pk-code-block), text (a string, or { text }).

props.name: runLabel
props.description: Text of the Run button. Defaults to "Run".

parts.name: form
parts.description: Wraps the fields and the Run button; submitting it (click or Enter) runs the action.

parts.name: fields
parts.description: Holds one control per config.input entry.

parts.name: outcome
parts.description: Holds the loading/error state while run() is in flight, then the drawn outcome.

a11y: Every field is a labelled real control (pk-input/pk-textarea/pk-select, showLabel on); the loading and error states use pk-skeleton and pk-alert's own roles and announcements.

examples.title: Word count (set config and run from script: an inline script cannot run under this site's CSP, so wire it the way pk-command-palette's items are wired)
